clues.kinetics: Absolute oral bioavailability is 74%, and a high-fat meal leaves exposure unchanged though peak concentration falls by 32%. About 40% is protein bound, and roughly 70% is cleared by the liver with 30% by the kidney.
clues.substance: Formulated as a citrate salt, and the parent compound has a molecular weight of 312.37.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA in 5 and 10 mg tablets, 11 and 22 mg extended-release tablets and a 1 mg/mL solution, dosed once or twice daily.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, cardiovascular events and thrombosis. There are no contraindications, and serious infections are the most common serious reactions.
clues.indication: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis, active psoriatic arthritis, active ankylosing spondylitis and ulcerative colitis in adults who had an inadequate response or intolerance to TNF blockers.
clues.mechanism: It blocks intracellular enzymes that relay cytokine signals, preventing STAT phosphorylation and activation. Its most potent in vitro combination was JAK1/JAK3, with an IC50 of 56 nM.

tell: A 3-hour half-life for the immediate-release tablet, alongside a once-daily extended-release version, sets this JAK inhibitor apart.
